current_stances.position: Ubique maintains that affective and defensive expressions, including involuntary eye muscle contractions and associated lacrimation, represent evolutionarily continuous adaptive mechanisms operating across species under both emotional and non-emotional conditions.

Ubique holds that tear secretion is primarily triggered by strong involuntary contraction of the peri‑ocular muscles that compresses blood vessels, serving a protective function; emotional tears represent a later, culturally co‑opted use of this reflex.
